# Ezekiel 4 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** "And you, son of man, take a brick and lay it before you, and engrave on it a city, even Jerusalem.

**2** And put siege works against it, and build a siege wall against it, and cast up a mound against it. Set camps also against it, and plant battering rams against it all around.

**3** And you, take an iron griddle, and set it as an iron wall between you and the city. And set your face toward it, and let it be in a state of siege, and press the siege against it. This is a sign for the house of Israel.

**4** Then lie on your left side, and place the punishment of the house of Israel upon it. For the number of the days that you lie on it, you shall bear their punishment.

**5** For I assign to you a number of days, three hundred and ninety days, equal to the number of the years of their punishment. So long shall you bear the punishment of the house of Israel.

**6** And when you have completed these, you shall lie down a second time, but on your right side, and bear the punishment of the house of Judah. Forty days I assign you, a day for each year.

**7** And you shall set your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, with your arm bared, and you shall prophesy against it.

**8** And behold, I will place cords upon you, so that you cannot turn from one side to the other, till you have completed the days of your siege.

**9** And you, take wheat and barley, beans and lentils, millet and emmer, and put them into a single vessel and make your bread from them. During the number of days that you lie on your side, three hundred and ninety days, you shall eat it.

**10** And your food that you eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day; from day to day you shall eat it.

**11** And water you shall drink by measure, the sixth part of a hin; from day to day you shall drink.

**12** And you shall eat it as a barley cake, baking it in their sight on human dung."

**13** And the LORD said, "Thus shall the people of Israel eat their bread unclean, among the nations where I will drive them."

**14** Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! Behold, I have never defiled myself. From my youth up till now I have never eaten what died of itself or was torn by beasts, nor has tainted meat come into my mouth."

**15** Then He said to me, "See, I will let you have cow's dung instead of human dung, on which you may prepare your bread."

**16** Moreover, He said to me, "Son of man, behold, I will break the supply of bread in Jerusalem. They shall eat bread by weight and with anxiety, and they shall drink water by measure and in dismay.

**17** I will do this that they may lack bread and water, and look at one another in dismay, and waste away under their punishment.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Ezekiel 4.

- **4:8** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **4:10** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **4:11** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **4:15** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **4:17** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **4:16** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **4:1-3**: The brick-engraving and iron griddle create a prophetic tableau — a miniature siege model. The iron wall between prophet and city symbolizes YHWH's separation from Jerusalem.
- **4:5-6**: 390 days for Israel, 40 for Judah. The LXX reads 190 for Israel. The day-for-a-year principle (yom la-shanah) creates a symbolic chronology of sin.
- **4:14**: Ezekiel's protest echoes priestly purity concerns (Lev 11, 17:15). Unlike Jeremiah's objections, Ezekiel's is cultic — he guards his ritual cleanness even in exile.

### LOGOS
- **4:1-3**: Ezekiel's sign-acts are the most elaborate in prophetic literature. The clay brick model creates a visual sermon that bypasses verbal resistance — the exiles cannot avoid seeing it.
- **4:4-8**: The 390 + 40 days may correlate to the periods of the divided and united monarchies' sin. Physical suffering becomes a theological statement about the weight of national guilt.
- **4:12-15**: The human dung command and Ezekiel's successful protest reveal that even in prophetic obedience, the prophet's own moral boundaries are respected. God modifies the command.

### PNEUMA
- **4:1-3**: God tells Ezekiel to play out the coming siege of Jerusalem in miniature — scratching the city on a brick, building tiny siege works around it. It's street theater with a devastating message.
- **4:9-12**: Starvation rations made from a desperate mix of grains, baked over dung — this isn't just symbolic. This is exactly what people in a besieged city would experience. Ezekiel is living the prophecy.
- **4:14-15**: This is one of the few times a prophet successfully pushes back on God — and God actually changes the terms. Ezekiel's priestly conscience is respected even when he's being pushed to the edge.

— SOPHIA
